sources.name: Field Inspections — Inspections / Asset master
sources.description: Field-technician equipment inspections with photo evidence, plus the asset master they verify against. TEMPLATE — replace connection details, table/column names and REPLACE_* ids, keep the fraud annotations. For India, change domain.country to IN.

domain.notes: Starter template — equipment inspection, United States

datasets.name: Inspection records
datasets.description: One row per site inspection: claimed inspection date, asset site coordinates, photo evidence. Photo capture time + GPS are screened against the record automatically — the pack default radius for this vertical is 1 km (premise-bound), override with gps_radius_km if needed.

columns.name: asset_id
columns.description: Inspected asset — cross-case linked; serial-in-photo verifies against the asset master (verify_against, when OCR extraction is wired)

columns.name: inspection_date
columns.description: Claimed inspection date — a photo captured before it cannot show this inspection

columns.name: work_order_date
columns.description: Work-order issue date — an inspection dated before it is an impossible ordering (date rule below)

columns.name: condition_photo_url
columns.description: Condition/defect photo — reuse across inspections is the recycled-report signal

columns.name: equipment_manual_url
columns.description: Attached equipment manual/datasheet. ROLE supporting = never fingerprinted (the same manual on every inspection is expected, not fraud).

verify_against.name: serial_vs_asset_master
verify_against.description: the serial number read off the equipment photo must exist in the asset master — a wrong-asset photo cites a serial the register doesn't know (or a different site's unit)

datasets.name: Asset master
datasets.description: Asset register with serials and locations — the system of record a serial number read off an inspection photo verifies against. No fraud_screening block: silence means the master is never screened itself; it is a verification TARGET.
